CYCLE10 FREQUENCY-EPOCH TEST
Exact stress-tuple obstruction audit

Status
No exact counterexample with locally infinite H^{m-1} was found. The exact scalar and vector harmonic realizations force the good-center set into a harmonic zero set, which has locally finite H^{m-1}. This does not establish that the full abstract measure-valued stress system has that representation or local finiteness. The established abstract conclusion remains sigma-finite rectifiability.

Exact abstract input
On a connected open Omega in R^m, the allowed tuple is
  nu >= 0, f vector-valued, beta symmetric matrix-valued, mu signed,
  d = tr(beta),
  [nu f^T; f beta] >= 0,
  grad(nu)=2f, div(f)=d, div(beta)=grad(mu),
  2mu <= d, and |mu| <= C d locally.
The measures are locally finite Radon measures; the order inequalities are measure inequalities. The exact good-center input on B4 has Z⊂B1 Borel, H(x,r)>0 and 1/2<=P(x,r)<=N for every x∈Z and 0<r<2, with
  H(x,r)=integral psi_{x,r} d nu,
  A(x,r)=r^2 integral phi_{x,r} d mu,
  P(x,r)=A(x,r)/H(x,r).
No proof body from the candidate source is used here.

Exact scalar harmonic realization and frequency calculation
For any nonzero harmonic polynomial u on R^2, set
  nu=u^2 dx, f=u grad(u) dx,
  beta=grad(u) tensor grad(u) dx,
  mu=|grad(u)|^2/2 dx, d=|grad(u)|^2 dx.
Then the block measure is the rank-one PSD measure [u;grad(u)][u;grad(u)]^T dx,
  grad(nu)=2f,
  div(f)=|grad(u)|^2+u Delta u=d,
  div(beta)=grad(|grad(u)|^2/2)=grad(mu),
and 2mu=d, |mu|=d/2. Thus every listed order and distribution identity holds exactly.

For a homogeneous harmonic polynomial h_j(y-x) of degree j, radial integration by parts gives
  integral |grad h_j|^2 (1-|y-x|^2/r^2)^p dy
    = (2 p j/r^2) integral h_j^2 (1-|y-x|^2/r^2)^(p-1) dy.
With the prescribed kernels this means A_j(x,r)=(j/2)H_j(x,r). A harmonic polynomial expanded at x is a sum of homogeneous harmonic terms of degrees 0 through L. Distinct degrees are orthogonal under radial integration, so P(x,r) is a positive weighted average of j/2 over its nonzero Taylor terms. Consequently:
- if u(x)=0, its degree-zero term vanishes and 1/2<=P(x,r)<=L/2 for every r with room;
- if u(x)!=0, the degree-zero term dominates as r tends to zero, so P(x,r)->0.
Thus, for the exact kernel quotient, the good-center set of this model is precisely the zero set restricted to the stated interior/radius range.

INDEPENDENT ABSTRACT GOOD-CENTER RECTIFIABILITY BASELINE
=======================================================
Authoring status: language-model-assisted internal candidate proof.
Date: 2026-10-09. Worker: complexity_proof_recon, existing Sol/max.
No current broadcasting quantitative proof, or new sibling proof, read.
No harmonic-map representation is an assumption or a derived input here.
Historical priority, external validation, and formal verification: UNKNOWN.

0. Result, distinction from the older dimension theorem
-----------------------------------------------------
The claimed conclusion in this baseline is affirmative: under the exact
measure and frequency conventions below, the full good-center set is
countably (m-1)-rectifiable and has sigma-finite H^(m-1). This is stronger
than a Hausdorff-dimension bound. The proof first obtains finite critical
measure on countably many pieces; it never assumes that finiteness in order
to apply a rectifiability theorem.

The new mechanism is an augmented-center covariance estimate. A center z
is lifted to (2P(z,t),z), so varying frequencies are part of the covariance
rather than an additive error. A uniform SECOND eigenvalue gap for the
integrated PSD block then gives a best-(m-1)-plane estimate linear in the
frequency drop. A maximal-density normalization closes the packing step
using a primary discrete Reifenberg theorem. All centers, including
exceptional centers for arbitrary proposed center measures, are covered by
the same countable decomposition.

The older internally audited abstract dimension proof and previous own
work were available background. No conclusion from that proof is needed
as an axiom below. In particular, global positivity of every ball-height
is not imported: positivity is required only where a good-center frequency
is defined. Radial identities are derived directly from the distributions.

1. Exact theorem and notation
----------------------------
Let U=B_10 in R^m, m>=1. The local version on any connected open set follows
by countable room covers. Let nu and d be nonnegative locally finite Radon
measures, f an R^m-valued locally finite Radon measure, beta a symmetric
m-by-m locally finite Radon measure, and mu a signed locally finite Radon
measure. Require the matrix-valued measure

                  [ f    beta ]                              (1.1)
